# Instructions

Do good work.

## Agent notes (AGENTS.md)

- This project is an OKF v0.2 novel bundle under `story/`.
- Start from `story/index.md` and follow links; run `novel context <concept>` for a prepared slice. Read `story/plan.md` (agreed premise, cast, rules, divergence goals) and `story/knowledge.md` (who knows what, when) before planning or drafting — nothing may contradict them.
- Register slash commands with `/recon`, `/outline`, `/knowledge`, `/draft`, `/scene-check`, `/weave`, `/continue`, `/revise`, `/continuity`, `/query`, `/ask`, `/migrate`, and `/skeptic` when your agent supports them.
- Structured questions can be answered without an agent: `novel query timeline --tag season-3a`, `novel query when <date>`, `novel query character <name>`, `novel query search <terms>`, `novel query threads --dangling`. For outline work run `novel context --story`; before drafting a scene run `novel context <scene> --so-far` to see who already knows what.
- Use `novel rename`, `novel mv`, `novel set`, and `novel diff` for renames, moves, frontmatter edits, and reviewing your own bulk changes — never raw `mv`/`sed`. Get explicit approval before bulk-creating chapters or scenes.
- After upgrading novel-harness, run `novel doctor --fix`, then `/migrate` for any content warnings.
- Canon detail lives on the web: `novel query refs <concept>` lists transcript, recap, and wiki links to fetch with your web tool when a scene needs exact staging, voice, or dialogue.
- opencode projects also get subagents (story-planner, scene-drafter, scene-checker, knowledge-keeper, researcher, skeptic, continuity-checker), package skills, novel_* tools, and a validate-on-write plugin; Claude Code gets the subagents and skills.
